title: Can a learned per-person Markov chain over webcam frames fool a detector where a hand-written generator could not?
lede: does a learned Markov chain help? A first-order chain over 32 k-means frame states, fitted on one person's earlier windows, is still caught at AUROC 1.000 on their later windows (frame or Gaussian emissions); every feature group alone catches it at 0.75 to 1.00.
summary: A negative result. For each of 46 DUX webcam-signal people, a first-order Markov chain over k-means states of their first-half frames (K=32; K=4 to 128 tried once) generates windows either by drawing a real frame of the state or the state's centroid plus Gaussian noise. A boosted-tree detector separates the person's later windows from generated ones at AUROC 1.000 (3 seeds), for own-person and pooled-people chains, with and without the person's profile. Single feature-group detectors each catch it too: level 0.97, spread 0.97, roughness 1.00, autocorrelation 1.00, cross-channel correlation 0.79 (own chain, real-frame emission). Whole-window and 50-frame copies of the same person reach 0.57 to 0.65, so what the chain loses is window-scale structure, not frame statistics. Stylised: one form-filling context.
